A flaw was found in rsyslog. This vulnerability allows a local user to spoof sender identity and cause downstream log consumers to misattribute event origins. When the imuxsock module is configured with plain trusted-property annotation, it fails to properly escape process names and executable paths in log metadata. A local attacker can exploit this issue by sending log messages through the local log socket with crafted process names to inject forged identity attributes.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the ct0 request parameter of the delivery scripts is only required to start with http:// or https:// and is prepended unescaped to banner click URLs. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a delivery URL that executes JavaScript in the delivery origin when a visitor follows it. An active banner using the raw {clickurl} macro is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone banner-linking page (zone-include.php) does not cast the keys of the includebanner request array to integers. An authenticated manager, or a trafficker with the zone-linking permission, who owns the submitted website and zone can place SQL in an array key, which is concatenated unquoted into the banner-lookup query, resulting in time-based blind SQL injection bounded by the privileges of the application's database account.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, deleting an agency, advertiser, or publisher through affected API paths can leave the associated account and user session active because the deletion path does not load the entity's account identifier before cleanup. A user whose entity has been deleted can continue accessing pages of the orphaned account. Access to data belonging to another agency was not demonstrated.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, unauthenticated request parameters in ad delivery can cause reflected cross-site scripting. A crafted delivery URL places a macro token in the source or target parameter and malicious markup in the referer parameter. Macro replacement after initial input encoding can insert the unescaped markup into generated banner output, causing JavaScript execution in the delivery origin when a visitor follows the URL. An active banner is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, user-controlled entity names in XLS report exports can be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas. A user with permission to rename a zone can place a formula in the zone name, which is then included in another user's Conversion Tracking report. Opening the affected spreadsheet can evaluate the formula and alter displayed report contents.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an advertiser can put XML syntax in fields of its own video creative. Unescaped MediaFile attributes and CDATA terminators allow the advertiser to inject elements into VAST responses served for a publisher's zone. A crafted TrackingEvents block can suppress the ad server's video playback event records and redirect tracking requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager can supply another agency's advertiser or website identifier as a report scope and obtain that entity's name in an XLS report header. Submitted scope identifiers are not checked against the manager's permitted selections. The demonstrated disclosure is limited to entity names.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone-linking page can disclose campaign and banner names and identifiers belonging to another agency. An authenticated manager, or a website user with permission to link banners to zones, can supply another agency's advertiser and campaign identifiers because the selection lists are not restricted to the agency owning the zone.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the public conversion-variable endpoint does not verify that a caller-supplied conversion belongs to the supplied tracker. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a unique variable for a different tracker's conversion, causing that conversion to be classified as a duplicate and excluded from conversion reports.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager with access to two advertisers can associate a conversion tracker owned by one advertiser with a campaign owned by the other. The tracker-campaign page checks access to each object but does not verify that their actual owners match. The resulting association can expose the first advertiser's tracker name and identifier in the second advertiser's restricted conversion report.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the Search Agents API of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with Viewer privileges can send crafted requests to manipulate backend SQL queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the patch management functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with Viewer web access can perform administrative patch management operations. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

GNU mtools through 4.0.50 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability that allows attackers to crash mtools commands by supplying a FAT image with a zero sectors-per-cluster byte. Attackers can craft a FAT image that, when opened with mdir, minfo or mtype, triggers a SIGFPE in calc_num_clus() on x86, causing denial of service.

ICU4C through 79.1 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in the x11-compound-text converter because cloning shares the extraInfo block without a safeClone handler. Attackers who control the charset name passed to ucnv_open() in applications calling ucnv_setSubstString() or cloning converters can corrupt the heap, causing crashes and potentially code execution.

A vulnerability was detected in mahmoudai1 school-management-system up to ecec9faaf2fb1a3c5cd096e063f8ef326d09cdfd. The impacted element is the function userModel::checkUserInDB of the file loginServer.php of the component Login Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TOTOLINK N350RT 9.3.5u.6468_B20250827/9.3.5u.6466_B20250825. The affected element is the function setLanguageCfg of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. Such manipulation of the argument lang leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

A weakness has been identified in Spotweb up to 1.5.8. This issue affects the function redirect of the file lib/SpotTemplateHelper.php of the component Login. Executing a manipulation of the argument http_referer can lead to open redirect. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. This patch is called 0853d646d615225b35f466a960976d1492b786a9. Applying a patch is advised to resolve this issue.

An arbitrary file write vulnerability exists in the patch upload functionality of StellarOne due to improper validation of file paths. An attacker with admin web access can upload a crafted patch package to write arbitrary files on endpoints with the privileges of the endpoint service. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the vShell command-line interface of StellarOne due to improper validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with access to vShell can inject crafted commands to bypass the restricted shell environment and execute arbitrary operating system commands. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the patch apply functionality of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux) due to insufficient validation of uploaded patch packages before extraction. An attacker with low-privileged web access can upload a crafted patch package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An improper version validation vulnerability exists in the product update mechanism of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). An attacker with product admin privileges can downgrade the product to an older, potentially vulnerable version, potentially allowing previously patched vulnerabilities to be reintroduced and security protections to be weakened. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in an Accounts Manager service of StellarOne running inside a container due to improper handling of user-supplied input in SQL queries. An attacker with command execution access to the host system or another container with network connectivity to the affected service can send crafted requests to manipulate backend database queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the update functionality of StellarOne due to insufficient validation of files contained within uploaded update packages. An attacker with web administrator privileges can upload a crafted update package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An HTML injection vulnerability exists in the alert notification functionality of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of agent-supplied data. An attacker controlling an agent identity can submit crafted HTML content, potentially allowing the attacker to manipulate displayed content or deceive recipients. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the firmware update functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with admin privileges can upload a crafted firmware package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the system. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper access control vulnerability exists in a privileged Unix domain socket of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). Due to insufficient authorization checks, a low-privileged local attacker can interact with the daemon and invoke privileged operations without the necessary permissions. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

Friendica through 2026.05-1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in item_edit() that allows authenticated local users to edit other authors' posts by submitting their own stored copy's post_id. Attackers can POST to /item to delete attachments and overwrite the shared body, title and content warning, which is shown under the original author's name.

markdownify-mcp before 1.2.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass URL validation by supplying DNS names, bracketed IPv6 literals, or IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses. Attackers can influence URLs passed to webpage-to-markdown or git-repo-to-markdown through prompt injection to fetch loopback services, internal hosts, and cloud metadata endpoints.

wpa_supplicant 2.7 through 2.12 with the wolfSSL backend contains an EAP-FAST server authentication bypass in tls_sess_sec_cb() that skips master secret derivation for oversized PAC-Opaque tickets. Adjacent attackers running a rogue authenticator can complete the handshake with an all-zero master secret to capture MS-CHAPv2 responses for offline cracking and replace the stored PAC.

Grav Admin plugin before 1.10.65 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability in LoginController::taskForgot() that ignores the Require Trusted Host setting when building reset links. Unauthenticated attackers who know an administrator's username can submit the forgot-password form with a forged Host header, capturing the reset token when clicked to take over accounts.

Grav Form plugin before 9.2.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows page authors to write uploads into Twig template folders by setting an unchecked file field destination in Form::uploadFiles(). Attackers can upload .txt or .svg files containing Twig and have them rendered as trusted templates outside the sandbox, executing code as the web server user.

Kestra is an open-source control plane for workflows across data, infrastructure, and applications. Prior to version 2.0.1, the namespace-files export endpoint places an unvalidated namespace path segment into the Content-Disposition filename of the ZIP download. An attacker who tricks a user into following a crafted export URL can inject Content-Disposition header parameters to spoof the saved filename or extension. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

A flaw was found in Submariner. In its default Pre-Shared Key (PSK) mode, all gateways within a broker set utilize the same PSK. An attacker, by knowing this shared PSK, can forge an Endpoint Custom Resource (CR) to impersonate another cluster's identity. This enables the attacker to establish an Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) tunnel under the false identity, leading to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack on network traffic between clusters.

Gogs is an open source self-hosted Git service. Prior to 0.15.0, Gogs does not regenerate the session ID after successful authentication. An attacker who forces a victim to use a known session ID can hijack the session after the victim logs in and take over the account. This issue is fixed in version 0.15.0.

This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::LoadMD5MeshFile() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via unvalidated weight ranges and bone indices. Attackers can supply a crafted .md5mesh file with out-of-range mBone values to increment heap words past the piCount allocation, causing memory corruption, out-of-bounds reads, or crashes.

Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::MakeDataUnique() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying unvalidated face indices. Attackers can craft an .md5mesh file with out-of-range face vertex indices or unfilled faces to set bits past the abHad allocation, read vertex data out of bounds, or crash the application.

EverOS before 1.8.0 contains a cross-origin local file disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious websites to read local files by abusing a wildcard CORS policy with credentials and unrestricted file:// ingestion. Attackers can host JavaScript that calls POST /api/v2/memory/add with file:// URIs, then read parsed contents via POST /api/v2/memory/search to exfiltrate SSH keys, credentials, and alter or delete memories.

build-git-clone before 1.0.4 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the clone() function that allows attackers to execute commands by supplying crafted repository URLs. Attackers can embed shell metacharacters such as ; or $() in the url argument, which is concatenated into a sh -c command, to execute operating system commands with Node.js process privileges.

merge-deep-composed through 0.1.4 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in _mergeDeepOne() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ keys. Attackers can pass JSON-parsed input containing __proto__ as a merge source to inject inherited properties, causing logic bypass or denial of service in Node.js processes.

@oleksii-pavlov/deep-merge before 1.2.4 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in deepMergeTwoAssignable() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying a __proto__ key. Attackers can pass JSON-parsed input to deepMerge(), deepMergeAndAssign(), deepUpdate() or deepUpdateAndAssign() to inject inherited properties, causing logic bypass or denial of service.

@irrelon/path 6.2.2 before 7.0.3 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in merge() and mergeImmutable() that allows remote attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying __proto__ keys. Attackers can pass untrusted JSON containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype payloads to merged objects, causing property injection, authorization bypass, or denial of service.

Teracom TCW122B-CM firmware before 4.07 contains a predictable session cookie vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack administrator sessions by guessing tick-counter-derived cookies. Attackers can predict or brute-force the 32-bit cookie from device uptime and login timing to control relays, settings, and administrator credentials.

ProjeQtOr before 13.1.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in tool/getAFieldForAClassById.php that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read any object property. Attackers can request Class=User with an administrator id and field=password or email to retrieve password hashes for offline cracking.

NodeBB 4.12.0 before 4.16.4 contains an execution after redirect vulnerability in the Intents.create controller that allows unauthenticated attackers to trigger ActivityPub note ingestion. Attackers can send GET requests to /intents/create with a remote note URI in the toPid parameter to inject federated content as local topics and posts.

OpenCV 3.0.0 through 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 through 5.1.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the built-in MJPEG encoder when writing grayscale frames due to incorrect level shifting in convertToYUV(). Attackers controlling pixel content written as grayscale MJPEG video can trigger unchecked cat_table and huff_dc_tab lookups, leaking adjacent or uninitialized memory into the output file or crashing the process.

GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmlParseStartTag2() that allows attackers to crash applications by triggering parser context reuse after SAX1 parsing. Attackers can supply documents with attributes parsed first with XML_PARSE_SAX1 and then without it on a reused context, causing writes to unallocated ctxt->attallocs and denial of service.

Xiph.Org libFLAC 1.5.0 contains a memory leak in FLAC__stream_encoder_finish() because free_() never releases the main thread task's frame bit writer buffer. Attackers submitting many audio streams to a long-running service that reuses one encoder can leak at least 32 KiB per stream, causing memory exhaustion.

libical 4.0.0 before 4.0.7 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in icalrecur_iterator_set_range() that allows attackers to cause denial of service by supplying crafted recurrence rules. Attackers can provide a calendar whose recurrence rule is iterated over a reverse range, causing the loop to never terminate and spin the calling thread at full CPU indefinitely.

libvorbis through 1.3.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in _ov_getlap() in lib/vorbisfile.c that passes a negative sample count from vorbis_synthesis_lapout() to memcpy(). Attackers can supply a short, valid Ogg Vorbis file with suitable block sizes to overwrite stack frames and crash applications performing two consecutive lapped seeks.

Xiph.Org libvorbis through 1.3.7 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ov_time_tell() in lib/vorbisfile.c that reads vf->vi[-1].rate after a failed seek leaves vf->pcm_offset at -1. Attackers can supply a crafted Ogg Vorbis file with a corrupted page to applications that seek and query playback time, leaking heap bytes via the returned value or crashing the process.

FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds write in h264_context_reset() in libfreerdp/codec/h264.c, which stores new dimensions before the YUV planes are reallocated. Remote peers can trigger surface height increases so avc420_compress() writes taller frames past undersized luma and chroma planes, corrupting heap memory or crashing the process.

FFmpeg through 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because avcodec_flush_buffers() does not release the decoder context's frame buffer pool, so recycled buffers retain prior picture data. Attackers can supply crafted damaged streams to applications reusing one decoder context across users to recover another user's decoded picture content from unwritten frame regions.

GNOME libxml2 2.14.0 through 2.15.4 contains a missing NUL termination flaw in xmlBufferAddHead() in buf.c that leaves uninitialized heap bytes as the terminator for storage-less buffers. Attackers supplying data to applications reusing an xmlBuffer can trigger over-reads via xmlBufferCat() and xmlStrlen(), disclosing adjacent heap memory or causing crashes.

GNOME libxml2 2.12.6 through 2.15.4 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in xmlTextReaderConstEncoding() after a reader is reset with xmlReaderNewWalker(). Because xmlCtxtReset() leaves ctxt->input NULL, querying the document encoding makes xmlGetActualEncoding() read ctxt->input->flags without a check, crashing the application and causing denial of service.

GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a double free vulnerability in xmlReaderNewWalker() that frees reader->input again after xmlTextReaderClose() already released it. Applications reusing a closed xmlTextReader with xmlReaderNewWalker() can crash, and groomed heap memory can control the close callback for possible code execution.

GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger stale DTD validation states after xmlTextReaderCurrentDoc documents are freed. Attackers can supply an XML document ending with an error inside an element, causing xmlTextReaderClose to read freed element declarations, leading to crashes and possible invalid frees.

Boost.JSON 1.84.0 through 1.92.0 contains an information exposure vulnerability because parser_for reset() does not reset nested parse_into handlers, retaining state across documents. Attackers controlling an abandoned or subsequent document parsed by a reused parser_for can cause partial string data from one document to appear in another's result.

GEOS 3.13.0 before 3.15.1 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in RectangleContains::isContainedInBoundary that recurses indefinitely on curved geometries returned by getGeometryN. Attackers can supply crafted WKT or WKB CircularString, CompoundCurve, or CurvePolygon geometries tested via PreparedGeometry::contains or GEOSPreparedContains against a prepared rectangle to crash the process with a stack overflow.

libxml2 2.13.0 through 2.15.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability because xmlTextReaderSetup does not reset reader->state when a reader is reused. Attackers can submit one malformed XML document to an application reusing a single reader, causing every later document to be rejected until the reader is recreated.

libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by triggering xmlFreeNode on a stale reader->faketext node after xmlTextReader reuse. Attackers can supply XML containing a namespace declaration to applications that read its value and reuse the reader, causing a freed document's dictionary read and process crash.

GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement because xmlCtxtReset frees the DTD without popping stale validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document ending inside an element to an application reusing a DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads, causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error messages.

Loginizer before 2.1.4 contains a brute-force lockout bypass vulnerability in loginizer_login_failed() that allows unauthenticated attackers to avoid failed-attempt recording via non-ASCII URL bytes. Attackers can append invalid UTF-8 or 4-byte sequences to wp-login.php or xmlrpc.php request URLs, causing the log INSERT to fail and enabling unlimited password guessing without lockout or email notification.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows account administrators to attach integration hooks to other accounts' inboxes by supplying a foreign inbox_id. Attackers can create a Dialogflow hook referencing a victim inbox, leaving its new conversations stuck as pending awaiting a bot, and enumerate inbox IDs to disclose inbox names.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the Bandwidth SMS webhook endpoint POST /webhooks/sms/:phone_number that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit forged SMS events. Attackers who know an inbox phone number can set the 'to' field to inject inbound messages with forged sender numbers or forge delivery status updates.

Leptonica 1.79.0 through 1.87.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in l_byteaInitFromStream() that allows attackers to write past a heap buffer by supplying oversized input. Attackers can provide a file larger than 1,000,000,000 bytes, causing l_byteaCreate() to allocate a 201-byte buffer before memcpy copies the full stream size, crashing the application.

BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editors to permanently delete recycle bin content by converting chapters to books or books to shelves. Attackers can trigger TrashCan::destroyEntity() through the conversion actions to force-delete soft-deleted children, revisions and attachments, including content deleted by other users, preventing restoration.

Wallos before 5.11.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability that allows authenticated users or API key holders to exhaust server resources by storing subscriptions with a frequency of 0. Attackers can trigger renew.php or get_monthly_cost.php to loop forever on a P0D interval, pinning PHP workers and hanging the next-payment cron job for all users.

paramz through 0.10.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted model files to paramz.load(), which calls pickle.load() without restrictions. Attackers can embed objects whose __reduce__ method returns callables like exec or os.system in shared paramz or GPy model files to run code with the victim's privileges.

ToolJet from 3.16.0 before 3.20.256 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability in StripeWebhookGuard that validates webhooks against a self-generated signature instead of the Stripe-Signature header. Unauthenticated attackers can post forged Stripe events to the POST /api/organization/payment/webhooks route to activate subscriptions, generate licenses, change plans or seats, and add AI credits without payment.

Cron-parser through 5.10.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in CronExpressionParser.parse() that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by supplying oversized cron fields. Attackers can submit a roughly 1.6 MB expression of repeated wildcard tokens that expand into huge arrays, exhausting the V8 heap and crashing the Node.js process.

llama.cpp from b7118 before b12604 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in llama_grammar_parser::parse_sequence() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service by supplying GBNF repetitions with max lower than min. Attackers can send a grammar like {5,2} in the grammar field of a llama-server /completion request, wrapping n_opt to generate endless repetition rules that hang the process and exhaust memory.

DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0 contains a command execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands without user approval because the shellsafe classifier treats git blame and git whatchanged as read-only. Attackers can plant a diff textconv driver in .gitattributes and .git/config so that git blame, triggered via prompt injection or routine use, executes attacker-chosen commands with the user's privileges, exposing stored provider API keys and session history.

A weakness has been identified in EduardoPires EquinoxProject up to 1.10. This vulnerability affects the function BuildToken of the file src/Equinox.Services.Api/appsettings.Development.json of the component JWT Bearer Authentication. This manipulation of the argument SecretKey with the input fmFGn5agHZkuG2N0e1zaEJIQtGVoNN5P causes hard-coded credentials. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security flaw has been discovered in caoqianming django-vue-admin up to 849f9aafa552380c64eecc6059e357f6a1f5437a. This affects the function UserModifySerializer of the file server/apps/system/serializers.py. The manipulation results in dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The patch is identified as d0bc4cf6232798d1f977eb4cad03738a968c4869. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue.

This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session

CodeSafe is an open-source Python library for code encryption, decryption, and safe evaluation using Python's AST module. From versions 0.0.1 through 0.0.4, the safe_eval() function can be bypassed with indirect subscript calls such as builtins'exec', because AST validation blocks only direct calls to dangerous built-ins. An attacker who controls an expression passed to safe_eval() can execute arbitrary Python code with the permissions of the host application. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.5.

OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. From versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.18 and 3.5.0 through 3.5.2, decoding a crafted HT-compressed EXR chunk can cause ht_undo_impl() to write a 4-byte pixel value through a pointer that is not 4-byte aligned. This happens when the channels sum to a bytes-per-scanline stride that is not a multiple of four. This issue is fixed in versions 3.4.19 and 3.5.3.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.6.49 before 0.11.0, sandbox file extraction has no cumulative byte or file-count limit. A user who can run a code-execution block that extracts files can exhaust the memory of the shared workflow executor, interrupting other users' runs on it. Each file was allowed up to 50 MB based on a size that the sandbox itself reported. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.4 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that on instances with receptive cluster agents enabled could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to make requests to internal network services through the GitLab agent server due to insufficient validation of destination addresses.

A vulnerability was identified in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.7. Affected by this issue is the function fillModelFromData of the file src/Services/AdminService.php. The manipulation of the argument id/remember_token/enabled leads to dynamically-determined object attributes. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 4.7.8 can resolve this issue. The identifier of the patch is 9b0c98dc3e2710b2ba8d7579da89ec6a4042fcc8. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was detected in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.7. The impacted element is the function update of the file src/Services/AdminUserService.php of the component Admin User Management. The manipulation results in missing authorization. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 4.7.8 is sufficient to resolve this issue. The patch is identified as 70910338c1e136d5bdd6ed795768e7a81445f422. The affected component should be upgraded.

A security flaw has been discovered in slowlyo owl-admin up to 4.7.6. This issue affects the function saveData of the file src/Services/AdminUserService.php of the component User Management. Performing a manipulation of the argument roles results in missing authorization. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 4.7.7 is capable of addressing this issue. The patch is named 762a32a374f68cd2cbad12c0d710dcd537f3b127. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to send requests to internal network resources due to insufficient validation in repository import.

Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-15 contained a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to store markup in the profile full_name field by submitting a modified request directly to the backend, which persists the value without sanitization. The Contact Support workflow later inserts the stored name into the generated support email without HTML encoding, so attackers can make injected HTML and media, such as misleading banners, masked hyperlinks and external tracking resources, render in support messages received by the support team.

Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a client-supplied extracted_data object without verifying invoice ownership, enforcing the invoice_edit permission or checking whether the invoice has been soft deleted. Authenticated attackers who know an invoice identifier can overwrite seller and buyer details, invoice identifiers, product entries, totals and custom metadata of invoices, including archived invoices marked is_deleted = 1, undermining the integrity of fi

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to perform server-side request forgery against internal network resources due to insufficient URL validation in MCP server OAuth handling.

Glances is an open-source system cross-platform monitoring tool. In versions prior to 4.5.7, the on-alert action command tokenizer in secure.py treats quote characters as argument boundaries without escaping. A monitored stat value, such as a mount point name, that is quoted in an action command template can contain a quote character that breaks out of its quote boundary and injects additional arguments into the process the action invokes. No shell operator is needed for this attack. This issue has been fixed in version 4.5.7.

SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, FileStore.ValidatePassword in the SFTP server does not reject zero-length secrets before comparing them, causing an empty login password to match any account configured without one, such as public-key-only or certificate-only users. Because password authentication is enabled by default, a remote attacker who knows a valid username can log in without a key or secret and obtain an SFTP session with that user's home directory and path permissions. This issue is fixed in version 4.46.

SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, the S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on POST Object uploads, which are multipart/form-data POST requests to the bucket. An authenticated S3 identity that a bucket policy restricts, such as to a key prefix or by source IP, can create or overwrite objects it is denied by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT. This issue has been fixed in version 4.46.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.7 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing resource limits in the error tracking integration.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing server-side input validation on on-call rotation values.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that on instances with incoming email enabled could have allowed an authenticated user with CI job access to obtain sensitive information belonging to another user due to improper scope validation.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a fine-grained personal access token to read and apply merge request suggestions from projects outside the token's scope due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.11 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with developer-role permissions to self-approve their own merge request and merge code into protected branches due to incorrect authorization when a security policy prohibited author self-approval.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the LSUpdate.parse function of the NSE ospf.lua library, which does not advance when it reads an LSA header with a zero length. An attacker on the same layer 2 segment can send a single spoofed, unauthenticated OSPF LS Update packet, causing a permanent 100% CPU hang of the Nmap process as soon as broadcast-ospf2-discover.nse captures it.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in the TLV.AUTH parser of the NSE eigrp.lua library, whose length arithmetic cancels out the running read position. An attacker on the same layer 2 segment can send a single crafted EIGRP Update of roughly 36 bytes over unauthenticated multicast, causing unbounded table growth that exhausts the memory of the Nmap process when broadcast-eigrp-discovery.nse is running.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the dispatcher of the NSE tftp.lua library, which removes completed coroutines but not ones that ended in an error, leaving a zero-yield spin. A malicious TFTP exchange reached by snmp-ios-config.nse after an SNMP write sequence can leave a dead coroutine that freezes the entire Nmap invocation, before port scanning begins for any target in the run; the hang is prevented when the script-timeout option is set.
